How this example was made
  • Made on 2 October 2026 in one real Slide Lab run, on a fictional template (Meridian) with invented numbers. Nothing here is client material.
  • Storyline: written from a finished data sheet, 2 minutes. A real storyline conversation usually takes 10 to 30 minutes.
  • Designs: 10 slides with 3 options each, all designed at the same time, 13 minutes.
  • After the picks: converting them to editable PowerPoint took 25 seconds (no agent needed, including the growth loop); finalize and compile took under 2 minutes.
  • Quality check: 1 Major finding (the slide 5 chart axis started at $300M, which overstated the gap). Slide 5 was redesigned in 2 minutes and the deck recompiled; 6 Advisory items remain (mostly titles that wrap).
  • Hand edits, all disclosed: slide 6's footer placeholder was replaced with the deck's source line before review; slide 8's takeaway was shortened from 131 to 98 characters before the final check. Everything else is the pipeline's own output.

Dot-dash storyline: Southeast Asia Entry

Deck type
Business Case
Governing thought
Meridian should enter Southeast Asia through Vietnam first, then Indonesia, starting with $12M of Phase 1 funding.
Audience
Meridian's investment committee. They see Southeast Asia as attractive but risky, and lean toward either a large multi-market launch or waiting.
Belief to break
"Entering Southeast Asia means a big, all-at-once bet across the region."
Belief to leave with
"A capped $12M first step in Vietnam, with two stop points, tells us whether to scale before we commit more."
Room should say back
Approve $12M for Vietnam now; decide on Indonesia at month 18.
Read the slide headlines top to bottom: they should tell the deck's whole argument.
Slide 1 — Southeast Asia entry: Vietnam first
Meridian should enter Southeast Asia through Vietnam first, then Indonesia.
  • Title: Southeast Asia entry: Vietnam first
  • Tagline: A capped $12M first phase with two go/no-go gates
  • Subtitle: Recommendation to the Meridian investment committee
  • Presenter: Meridian Strategy Team
  • Date: November 2026
  • Audience / Client: Meridian investment committee
Slide 2 — Leading with Vietnam reaches a $40M run-rate in 18 months for $12M
Leading with Vietnam reaches a $40M revenue run-rate in 18 months for $12M.
  • WHERE TO START — Vietnam, then Indonesia: the only two of five markets that clear both the $1.0B market-size bar and the 3.5 readiness bar.
  • WHY NOW — The regional category doubles from $2.1B in 2024 to $4.2B in 2030, and Vietnam passes Thailand as a market in 2027.
  • HOW WE WIN — A five-step, partner-led playbook, proven in one city before national rollout, then reused in Indonesia.
  • WHAT IT COSTS — $12M for Phase 1, capped until Gate 2, for a $40M revenue run-rate within 18 months.
  • ALTERNATIVES REJECTED — Thailand first fails the size bar ($0.8B by 2030); launching in all five at once spreads $12M too thin to prove anything.
  • THE ASK — Approve $12M of Phase 1 funding by 15 Nov 2026; decide on Indonesia at month 18.
Slide 3 — The Southeast Asia market doubles to $4.2B by 2030
The Southeast Asia category market doubles to $4.2B by 2030.
  • 12% A YEAR — The category grows from $2.1B in 2024 to $4.2B in 2030, about 12% a year.
  • TWO MARKETS DRIVE IT — Vietnam (18% a year) and Indonesia (15% a year) grow fastest and make up $2.5B of the 2030 total.
  • MATURE MARKETS LAG — Thailand (6%) and Malaysia (5%) grow at under half the regional rate.
Slide 4 — Only Vietnam and Indonesia clear both the size and readiness bar
Only Vietnam and Indonesia clear both the size and the readiness bar.
  • THE BAR — A market must reach at least $1.0B by 2030 and score at least 3.5 out of 5 on readiness (partners, distribution, rules for foreign brands).
  • VIETNAM PASSES — $1.2B by 2030, 18% a year, readiness 4.0 (partners 4, distribution 4, rules 4).
  • INDONESIA PASSES — $1.3B by 2030, 15% a year, readiness 3.7 (partners 4, distribution 4, rules 3).
  • THAILAND FAILS ON SIZE — Ready (4.0) but only $0.8B by 2030, growing 6% a year.
  • PHILIPPINES AND MALAYSIA FAIL BOTH — $0.5B and $0.4B by 2030, readiness 2.7 and 3.3.
Slide 5 — Vietnam passes Thailand in 2027 and the gap keeps widening
Vietnam passes Thailand as a market in 2027 and the gap keeps widening.
  • THAILAND LEADS TODAY — In 2024 Thailand is the larger market, $564M against Vietnam's $444M.
  • CROSSOVER IN 2027 — Vietnam reaches $729M in 2027, passing Thailand's $672M.
  • 1.5 TIMES BY 2030 — Vietnam reaches $1,200M against Thailand's $800M.
  • WHY VIETNAM BEFORE INDONESIA — Similar size, but Vietnam grows faster (18% against 15% a year) and is more ready (4.0 against 3.7), so it is the safer first proof.
Slide 6 — A five-step playbook takes each market from partner search to scale
A five-step playbook takes each market from partner search to scale.
  • 1 PICK THE PARTNER — Choose and sign one local distribution partner with reach into modern and traditional trade.
  • 2 PROVE IT IN ONE CITY — Launch in Ho Chi Minh City first and track sell-through against target.
  • 3 PASS THE GATE — Scale only if the pilot meets its sell-through target; otherwise stop or fix.
  • 4 SCALE NATIONALLY — Roll out across the country with the partner once the unit economics hold.
  • 5 REUSE IN THE NEXT MARKET — Run the same five steps in Indonesia, starting with what Vietnam taught.
Slide 7 — The 18-month plan has two go/no-go gates before spending scales
The 18-month plan has two go/no-go gates before spending scales.
  • MONTHS 1-3 · PARTNER — Choose and sign the Vietnam distribution partner.
  • MONTHS 4-6 · PILOT — Pilot in Ho Chi Minh City.
  • MONTH 6 · GATE 1 — Continue only if pilot sell-through is at or above target.
  • MONTHS 7-12 · ROLLOUT — National rollout in Vietnam.
  • MONTH 12 · GATE 2 — Continue only if contribution margin is at least 15%.
  • MONTHS 13-18 · INDONESIA PREP — Indonesia partner search and entry preparation, with the Phase 2 funding decision at month 18.
Slide 8 — Local partners power a growth loop that makes each next market cheaper
Local partners power a growth loop that makes each next market cheaper.
  • MORE PARTNERS — Each market adds a distribution partner and its retailer relationships.
  • WIDER DISTRIBUTION — More outlets carry Meridian products sooner.
  • MORE SALES DATA — Wider distribution gives earlier, more detailed sell-through data.
  • BETTER TARGETING — The data shows which products, prices and channels work.
  • CHEAPER NEXT ENTRY — The next market starts from proven choices, so it costs less to enter, which attracts more partners.
Slide 9 — Spending stays capped at $12M until Gate 2 proves the unit economics
Spending stays capped at $12M until Gate 2 proves the unit economics.
  • LAUNCH MARKETING IS THE LARGEST PART — $4.0M, a third of the total.
  • SET-UP COSTS — Partner onboarding $2.5M and distribution set-up $3.0M.
  • TEAM AND BUFFER — A local team of $1.5M and $1.0M of contingency.
  • PHASE 2 IS SEPARATE — Indonesia is a new funding decision at month 18, not part of this $12M.
Slide 10 — Approve $12M of Phase 1 funding by 15 November 2026
Approve $12M of Phase 1 funding by 15 November 2026.
  • Primary ask: Approve $12M of Phase 1 funding for the Vietnam entry by 15 Nov 2026.
  • Sub-asks:
  • PARTNER SIGNED — Head of International signs the Vietnam distribution partner by 31 Jan 2027.
  • PILOT LAUNCHED — Vietnam general manager launches the Ho Chi Minh City pilot by 1 Mar 2027.
  • GATE 1 REVIEW — Investment committee reviews pilot sell-through in Jun 2027.
  • IF THE ANSWER IS NO — Meridian waits; the category doubles by 2030 and Vietnam passes Thailand in 2027 without us.
